source.title: PRODUCTIVE-MACHINE-PLATFORM-001: design open, locally serviceable productive machines
source.body:
## Parent and composition

This is the cross-cutting machine-engineering owner for:
- [APPLIANCE-MICROFACTORY-001 #6603](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/issues/6603): first appliance product cell and make/buy/partner routes.
- [DISTRIBUTED-APPLIANCE-FAB-001 #6735](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/issues/6735): admitted parts and household/neighbourhood production tiers.
- [CITYKIT-SYNTH-001 #3768](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/issues/3768) and [ABOVEGROUND-PANELCELL-001 #3773](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/issues/3773): productive capability closure and task-specific production-cell benchmarks.
- [EV-FACTORY-DESIGN-001 #2354](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/issues/2354): generic modular-factory economics and architecture.
- Symthaea [MFG-PROC-000 #5686](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/5686): process, capability, recipe and qualification semantics.
- Existing machine/robot safety, process control, Mycelix provenance, and repairability owners remain authoritative.

This issue composes those owners. It must not create a second MES, inventory ledger, process ontology, machine-control authority, robot dispatcher or provenance store.

## Objective

Design a family of **open, locally serviceable productive machines** that enable households, neighbourhood hubs, SMMEs and regional partners to fabricate, assemble, inspect, repair and eventually reproduce useful products and selected production equipment.

The programme is broader than distributing desktop 3D printers. It includes additive, subtractive, textile, electronics assembly/test, materials recovery, metrology, workholding and small-batch assembly. Each process remains a separately engineered machine with its own hazard controls and qualification. Shared interfaces are for documentation, identity, telemetry, maintenance, calibration and capability evidence—not a universal machine that combines incompatible hazards.

## Paradigm shift

Move from buying disconnected machines to deploying **evidence-bearing productive capability**:

1. A machine is a maintained production capability with a declared envelope, skills, feedstocks, utilities, safety controls, calibration state, maintenance state, output quality and accepted-output history—not just a model number or motion controller.
2. Product, process, machine, fixture, material and inspection are co-designed. Fixtures and test stations are production assets, not afterthoughts.
3. Standardise interfaces and evidence, not every physical mechanism. FDM, CNC, textile, polymer recovery and electronics processes should not be forced into one chassis.
4. Design machines for repair, local sourcing, replacement subassemblies, open documentation, second-source components and graceful manual operation.
5. Make production closure honest: a machine is not locally reproducible merely because its CAD is public. Its inputs include structural materials, motion components, electronics, bearings, motors, firmware, tooling, skills, power, safety controls, calibration and independent acceptance.
6. Optimise cost per accepted useful output and verified service restoration—not printer ownership, nominal speed, theoretical maximum throughput or a single self-sufficiency score.
7. Make the machine's own lifecycle observable: commissioning, calibration, tool wear, downtime, faults, maintenance, firmware/configuration changes, safety interlock checks and end-of-life recovery all produce version-bound evidence.

## First machine family — staged reference designs

### M0 — productive workbench and metrology/assembly station

Build this first as the enabling station: stable bench and workholding, calibrated hand tools, torque-controlled fastening, ESD controls where needed, low-voltage electrical test, dimensional inspection, scales, labels/serial identity, guarded fixtures and a documented calibration register. It supports assembly, repair and measurement before we invest in powered fabrication equipment.

### M1 — LMF-FDM-300: enclosed CoreXY material-extrusion printer (reference design)

Use a 300 mm-class XYZ build envelope as a design target, not a finished specification. It should be a serviceable frame/gantry/bed/electronics architecture using commonly sourceable extrusions, rails, belts, bearings, fasteners and replaceable subassemblies. Critical structural members and safety-related components must be metal or qualified bought components; printed parts are limited to non-critical covers, ducts, cable guides and other explicitly reviewed uses.

Required design work:
- frozen requirements and use-case envelope before detailed sizing;
- sourceable BOM with at least two supply paths for critical commodity components where feasible;
- frame/gantry stiffness and modal/thermal design calculations;
- kinematic and belt/lead-screw layout, tolerance stack and service access;
- enclosure, thermal runaway protection, over-temperature cut-outs, guarded hot surfaces/moving axes, interlocks and emergency-stop design as applicable;
- source-controlled emissions/ventilation plan, validated for the selected materials/process; no presumption that a generic enclosure or filter is sufficient;
- controlled firmware, machine configuration, calibration and process-profile releases;
- commissioning artefacts and geometric test coupons;
- maintenance plan, replaceable modules, wiring diagrams and independent build guide.

Use an established open design such as Voron as a *benchmark and learning baseline* before deciding which geometry to reuse or redesign. Confirm the exact upstream licence and comply with its conditions before adapting or distributing derived CAD. Do not claim a novel printer architecture without a matched benchmark.

### M2 — LMF-CNC-400: enclosed bench CNC router (later R2/N1 machine)

Develop only after the FDM and workholding/test cell is stable. Initial scope is bounded machining of suitable wood and plastics; metal cutting is not assumed. It requires a sufficiently rigid structure, spindle/tooling envelope, chip/dust extraction, enclosure, guarding, interlocked access, safe stop, workholding, tool/runout checks, geometric/positioning and thermal tests. CNC operation is not a household H0 process by default.

### M3 — LMF-RECYCLE-01: polymer sorting/recovery line (N1/R2 only)

A separate, guarded sequence: identified polymer intake and quarantine → cleaning/drying → controlled size reduction → melt/extrusion/filtration → spool or mould output → batch testing. Feedstock identity, contamination, degradation, melt-flow and mechanical-property drift must be measured. Do not mix unknown polymers or represent recycled feedstock as equivalent to virgin material. Shredder, extruder and press equipment require dedicated machine risk assessments and competent operators; no household build/use assumptions.

### M4 — textile and electronics repair/assembly cells

Use established sewing/textile and low-voltage electronics equipment first, then develop fixtures and semi-automation where measured bottlenecks justify it. Do not design mains electrical repair or safety-critical electronics into the first home toolkit.

## Common machine capability profile

Every machine release should provide a machine capability package referencing existing owner identities, with:
- machine ID, design revision, configuration/BOM digest and license;
- intended role, process type, capability tier, operating domain and explicitly prohibited uses;
- safety risk assessment, safeguarding architecture, safety-related functions and test/inspection procedures;
- facility, operator competence, required utilities, environmental and emission controls;
- materials/feedstocks, supplier/lot and conditioning requirements;
- tool, fixture, sensor and calibration identities/status;
- firmware/software/controller versions and signed/configuration digests;
- rated/validated process envelope, limits, uncertainty and known failure modes;
- maintenance intervals, spare parts, repair procedure and fault/recovery log;
- reference test artefacts, measurement methods, acceptance criteria and raw results;
- accepted-output cost, yield, downtime, energy/material and full labour denominators;
- commissioning, verification, independent replication and review/expiry evidence.

A CAD digest proves file identity, not engineering correctness. A machine self-report is not independent acceptance. An E-stop button or software interlock is not a complete machinery safety case.

## Benchmark contract

Compare each Luminous reference machine against at least one strong commercial baseline and one open-hardware baseline where those exist. Freeze use case, materials, test geometry, environment, operator skill, instrumentation, firmware and acceptance methods. Publish complete denominators and uncertainty.

Core dimensions:
- cost per accepted useful output, including capital, failed output, maintenance, calibration, energy, material, labour, ventilation, finishing, inspection, downtime and warranty/rework;
- first-pass yield and final yield, rework and scrap;
- output capability and dimensional/geometric error with uncertainty;
- process rate and useful throughput, not catalogue maximum speed;
- energy and consumables per accepted output;
- uptime, MTBF/MTTR, service access and common spare availability;
- operator training time, task burden and accessibility;
- repeatability across at least three independently operated nodes;
- traceability, rights/licence completeness, machine/process compatibility and rejection of seeded invalid conditions;
- safety-control availability, interlock proof-test results, exposure controls and near-miss/incident reporting.

Initial hypotheses, not achievements:
- 100% of released machine packages include source files, license, BOM, assembly/repair guide, risk file, wiring/control diagrams and commissioning protocol.
- 100% of critical purchased components have traceable identity/specification and at least one alternate sourcing path or an explicit single-source risk.
- three independent builds of one reference machine configuration, including two builders other than the design author where feasible.
- 100% rejection of seeded wrong configuration, stale calibration, unsupported tool/material, bypassed guard/interlock, unverified firmware/configuration and failed test cases.
- for a frozen low-volume work basket, target >=25% lower P50/P90 request-to-accepted-output or repair-restoration time versus a matched current route, with no safety, quality, recurrence or total-cost regression.
- compare household ownership, shared N1 hub access, R2 partner routing and OEM supply at annual demand 1/3/10/50/100.
- no Cpk claim until statistical stability and an adequate sample are demonstrated; report raw distributions and uncertainty first.

## Standards and technical references to consider

- ISO 12100:2010 — machinery risk assessment and risk reduction. As of 22 November 2026 the ISO catalogue lists it as current while ISO/DIS 12100.3 is under development; re-check status before design freeze.
- IEC 60204-1:2016+A1:2021 — electrical equipment of machinery, including protective bonding, overcurrent protection, emergency stop and technical documentation.
- ISO 230-1:2012 — geometric accuracy tests for machine tools under no-load or quasi-static conditions; it is not a complete operational performance or safety test.
- ISO/ASTM 52902:2023 — geometric capability test artefacts for additive systems.
- ISO/ASTM 52920:2023 — industrial AM processes and production sites; use as a regional-hub reference.
- ISO/ASTM 52951:2026 — AM part data-package/digital-thread model; detailed requirements are based on PBF-LB/M, so do not claim FDM conformity.
- ISO/ASTM 52966:2026 — AM capability levels for temporary self-sufficient systems; an architectural reference, not household machine certification.
- ISO 27548:2024 and NIOSH 2024-103 — desktop material-extrusion particle/chemical emissions and risk-control considerations.

## South African ecosystem strategy

Connect rather than duplicate:
- CSIR ADMIC describes polymer/powder additive manufacturing, 3D scanning, design optimisation and product lifecycle management for industry and SMMEs.
- CSIR Future Production: Manufacturing describes local advanced manufacturing, equipment, materials, industrialisation and SMME infrastructure.
- CSIR Centre for Robotics and Future Production describes automated inspection, customised robotic equipment, machine monitoring, benchmarking and skills development.
- CSIR CPAM is a relevant R&D pathway, but the located 2025/26 industry-led call closed 18 February 2026; no current grant window or eligibility is assumed.
- Precious Plastic is a relevant open-hardware precedent for local machine building and plastic recovery. Its own published account describes laser-cut components producible through local metal shops, with CAD/BOM/build instructions distributed. Treat project adoption counts as self-reported.
- Use local job shops for sheet cutting, machining, welding, coating and metrology until measured demand supports vertical integration.

No relationship, access agreement, supplier quote, grant eligibility or physical capacity is assumed from this discovery list.

## Execution sequence and gates

1. Freeze the machine family architecture, boundaries and common capability package.
2. Create M0 workbench/measurement station requirements and tool/calibration register.
3. Define LMF-FDM-300 user requirements, hazard register, mechanical concept, BOM and baseline plan.
4. Review a complete open-hardware baseline (including licence) and define matched commercial/open comparators.
5. Build and render the parametric envelope CAD. Treat it as a concept until engineering calculations, drawings, tolerance stack, risk file and independent review are complete.
6. Commission on a bench with no production claim; verify safety functions, movement, thermal behavior, geometric capability, emissions controls and repeatability separately.
7. Produce low-risk jigs/accessories under #6735 admission rules and test one cross-node reproduction.
8. Start CNC and recycling designs only as separate process-specific work packages after their safety and economic gates.
9. Publish actual supplier quotes, fabrication receipts, build logs and test data before any cost, local-content or SOTA superiority claim.

## Claim ceiling

This issue and its initial CAD are research/design outputs only. They do not establish a fabricated machine, safe machine, compliant equipment, qualified process, verified emissions, production capability, local content, supplier agreement, or commercial advantage. All performance targets are hypotheses until supported by physical measurements and independent review.
